chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sadeyr, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The believers are upon levels; some are upon one, some upon two, some upon three, some upon four, some upon five, some upon six, and some upon seven. So if you were to burden two upon the owner of the one, he would not be strong enough (for it); and three upon the owner of the two, he would not be strong enough; and four upon the owner of the three, he would not be strong enough; and five upon the owner of the four, he would not be strong enough; and six upon the owner of the five, he would not be strong enough; and seven upon the owner of the six, he would not be strong enough. And these are the levels.'
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the different spiritual levels of believers?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) elucidates the concept of 'tadarruj' (gradualism) in spiritual development, noting that believers occupy varying stations of faith and capacity. He illustrates that imposing duties or expectations beyond one's current spiritual station leads to weakness, emphasizing the necessity of assessing individual readiness before assigning higher responsibilities. This principle underscores the Shia scholarly understanding of divine wisdom in tailoring guidance to the diverse capacities of the community.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sadeyr who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said to me: ‘The Momins are upon levels. From them are ones upon one, and from them are ones upon two, and from them are ones upon three, and from them are ones upon four, and from them are ones upon five, and from them are ones upon six, and from them are one upon seven. So if you were to go and burden two upon the owner of the one he would not be strong enough (for it), and (burden) three upon the owner of the two he would not be strong enough (for it), and (burden) four upon the owner of the three he would not be strong enough (for it), and (burden) five upon the owner of the four he would not be strong enough (for it), and (burden) six upon the owner of the five he would not be strong enough (for it), and (burden) seven upon the owner of the six he would not be strong enough (for it). These are the levels’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from Sadir who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to me, ’Believers are of various positions in connection with belief. There are those who have one degree of belief, others have two degrees, still others may have three or four, five, six or seven degrees of belief. If you expect two degrees of belief from one who has only one degree of belief he is not able to bear it, or expect three degrees of belief from the one who has only two degrees of it he also is not able to bear it. The one who may have three cannot bear four degrees of belief, the one who has four degrees of belief is not able to bear five degrees of belief. One who has only five degrees of belief is not able to bear six degrees of belief and one who has six degrees of belief is not able to bear seven degrees of belief. This is how the degrees of belief are.’”
